## Assessment verified

The failure chain, confirmed in source:

1. **Factory requires the field** — `extensions/factory/src/workflow.ts` (`IMPL_SCHEMA`, worker prompts) mandates `workLeftUndone` (and `decisionsRequiringApproval`) in the worker's handoff, with `WORKER_ACCEPTANCE = { level: "checked", ... }`.
2. **pi-subagents rejects it** — the `structured_output` tool takes *two* objects: `value` (validated against the factory schema, which allows `workLeftUndone`) and `acceptanceReport` (validated by pi-subagents itself). In `subagent-prompt-runtime.js:605` → `validateAcceptanceReport` → `normalizeAcceptanceReportValue` (`src/runs/shared/acceptance.js:690`), any key not in `ACCEPTANCE_REPORT_FIELDS` (line 586 — `criteriaSatisfied, changedFiles, testsAddedOrUpdated, commandsRun, validationOutput, residualRisks, noStagedFiles, diffSummary, reviewFindings, manualNotes`) throws:
   `Invalid structured output acceptance report: acceptanceReport.workLeftUndone: unsupported acceptance report field` — the child dies at the acceptance handoff.

Two more traps in the same field set: `decisionsRequiringApproval` is also unsupported, and the acceptance report's `commandsRun` entries need `{command, result: "passed"|"failed"|"not-run", summary}` — not the `{command, exitCode}` shape the value schema wants. The fix belongs in the factory's worker prompts (pi-subagents is a pinned dependency), teaching the two-channel contract:

# Factory (`/factory`)

A minimal, reliable software factory. `/factory <task>` launches a bounded, asynchronous software-delivery pipeline and keeps the parent Pi session as the orchestrator.

## Pipeline

```
build workflow    scout → plan → implement (single writer, checked acceptance handoff)
deterministic     human-authored validation commands from .pi/factory.json
review workflow   3 parallel fresh reviewers (correctness, tests, simplicity)
                  → at most ONE fix pass, only on structured "fix" verdicts
deterministic     the same trusted commands, rerun as final verification
```

- Scout, planner, and reviewers run with fresh context and read-only toolsets; the implement and fix workers are the only writers (one at a time).
- Every machine-consumed child result uses a structured output schema, and branching happens **only** on the structured verdict — never on reviewer prose.
- The plan or implement stage stopping with unresolved human-owned decisions pauses the factory (`needs_approval`) instead of proceeding.
- Malformed or missing structured output fails the stage closed (`needs_attention`), never onward as success.
- The fix loop is capped at exactly one pass by construction. Failed deterministic checks also stop the factory — no automated retry of side-effectful work.
- **No commit, push, merge, publish, deploy, or release is ever performed.**

Execution, lifecycle, missions, artifacts, status, resume, and Herdr integration are owned by the installed [pi-subagents](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents) package; this extension only validates the baseline, generates the two fixed workflows, correlates RPC replies, and runs the deterministic checks.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/factory <task>` | Validate trust/baseline/config, then launch the build workflow asynchronously. |
| `/factory-status` | Show the latest run: swimlane waterfall, live workflow state, checks, reviewer disposition, decisions, errors. |

Baseline requirements: trusted project, inside a git work tree, clean working tree (unless `allowDirtyBaseline` is enabled), and `.pi/factory.json` present and valid.

Human-authored project configuration. It is the **only** source of validation commands the factory will ever execute; commands proposed by model output are never run. Unknown fields and malformed values fail closed.

  # Factory (`/factory`)
  A minimal, reliable software factory. `/factory <task>` launches a bounded, asynchronous software-delivery pipeline and keeps the parent Pi session as the orchestrator.
  ## Pipeline
  ```
  build workflow    scout → plan → implement (single writer, checked acceptance handoff)
  deterministic     human-authored validation commands from .pi/factory.json
  review workflow   3 parallel fresh reviewers (correctness, tests, simplicity)

  deterministic     the same trusted commands, rerun as final verification
  ```

  - Every machine-consumed child result uses a structured output schema, and branching happens **only** on the structured verdict — never on reviewer prose.
  - The plan or implement stage stopping with unresolved human-owned decisions pauses the factory (`needs_approval`) instead of proceeding.

# Code Context — Stage end-time logic (factory waterfall)

Scope: how each lane's start/end is captured, stored, and rendered; which failure
paths leave/wrongly set an end time; the exact path that produced the red
`failed — build workflow did not complete` banner. No files edited.

## Files Retrieved
1. `extensions/factory/index.ts` (lines 63, 160–260, 385–575, 659–805) — span lifecycle (`openSpan`/`setSpanState`/`closeSpan`/`closeAllOpenSpans`), status polling, completion handlers, banner.
2. `extensions/factory/src/waterfall.ts` (lines 15–75, 118–175, 200–215) — span model, `chartRows`, `renderWaterfall`, `laneStateFromStatuses`.
3. `extensions/factory/src/state.ts` (lines 40–75, 195–240) — `FactorySpanRecord`, validation, `childStructuredOutput` (uses `"completed"`).
4. `extensions/factory/src/rpc.ts` (lines 45–95) — `status`/`spawn` RPC transport (returns `text` only).
5. `tests/factory/waterfall.test.ts` (lines 145–176) — parser/lane-state tests (use `"complete"`).
6. `tests/factory/state.test.ts` (lines 45–52) — completion payload fixtures (use `"completed"`).
7. `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/run-status.js` (lines 137–145, 640–660) — real status text shape.
8. `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/subagent-executor.js` (lines 5784, 5895–5901, 6127) — live workflow step status values.
9. `~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/pi-subagents/src/shared/types.d.ts` (line 32) — `WorkflowNodeStatus` includes `"completed"`.

## Key Code

### Span lifecycle — `extensions/factory/index.ts`
```ts
172  const relNow = (): number => Math.max(0, Date.now() - runStartMs());
174  const openSpan = (key, startMs = relNow()) => {
176      const existing = state.spans.find(s => s.key === key);
177      if (existing) return;                       // start captured ONCE, never refined
179      state.spans.push({ key, ..., startMs, endMs: null, state: "running" });
182  const setSpanState = (key, spanState) => {
184      if (span && span.endMs === null) span.state = spanState;   // does NOT close
187  const closeSpan = (key, finalState, endMs = relNow()) => {
189      if (span && span.endMs === null) { span.endMs = endMs; span.state = finalState; }
196  const closeAllOpenSpans = (finalState) => {
197      for (const span of state?.spans ?? []) closeSpan(span.key, finalState);  // every open lane -> SAME relNow()
```
`closeSpan` defaults `endMs` to `relNow()` (wall clock at the moment the code
observes the terminal state), so end times are recorded live, not derived from
the child's real completion instant. `closeAllOpenSpans` stamps *every* still-open
lane with the same instant.

### Status → lane mapping — `extensions/factory/index.ts:228`
```ts
228  const applyWorkflowStatus = (phase, text) => {
231      const laneFor = key => phase === "build"
             ? (key==="scout"||key==="plan"||key==="implement" ? key : undefined) : ...;
235      const statuses = parseWorkflowChildStatuses(text);
239      const laneState = laneStateFromStatuses(sts);
240      openSpan(lane);
241      if (laneState === "running" || laneState === "queued") setSpanState(lane, laneState);
242      else closeSpan(lane, laneState);            // only terminal states close here
```

### Lane state aggregation — `extensions/factory/src/waterfall.ts:204`
```ts
204  export function laneStateFromStatuses(statuses: string[]): WaterfallState {
205      if (statuses.includes("failed")) return "failed";
206      if (statuses.includes("paused")) return "attention";
207      if (statuses.every(s => s === "complete" || s === "stopped")) return "success";
208      if (statuses.includes("running")) return "running";
209      return "queued";
210  }
```
Only `"complete"`/`"stopped"` count as finished. pi-subagents live status uses
`"completed"` (see below), so a finished child aggregates to `"queued"`.

### Renderer — `extensions/factory/src/waterfall.ts`
```ts
124  const maxEnd = Math.max(...rows.map(s => s.endMs ?? 0), 0);
125  const maxMs  = Math.max(1, model.nowMs ?? maxEnd);
126  const now    = Math.min(maxMs, model.nowMs ?? maxMs);
130  const pos = ms => Math.min(chartW, Math.round((ms / maxMs) * chartW));
153  const end = span.endMs ?? now;                 // open lane -> now
159  const dur = ` ${formatDuration(Math.max(0, end - span.startMs))}${span.endMs === null ? "…" : ""}`;
```
Bars and duration both use `endMs`; the axis max is `model.nowMs` (the extension
passes `relNow()` on every refresh, `index.ts:206`/`:804`).

### Real pi-subagents status token — external evidence
`run-status.js:137-145` builds `Workflow child <workflowKey>:` lines;
`run-status.js:655` appends `step.status`. Live workflow steps are set to
`"completed"`:
```js
// subagent-executor.js:5784 / :6127
step.status = progress.status === "completed" ? "completed"
            : progress.status === "failed" ? "failed" : "running";
```
and `types.d.ts:32` `WorkflowNodeStatus = ... | "completed" | ...`.
The factory's own completion-payload reader agrees it is `"completed"`:
`state.ts:childStructuredOutput` checks `status === "completed"`, and
`tests/factory/state.test.ts:49-50` uses `status: "completed"`.

## Architecture (end-time data flow)
1. `/factory` seeds one coarse `build` span at `startMs: 0` (`index.ts:750`).
2. `schedulePoll` fires every 3 s (`index.ts:262-275`); `pollOnce` calls the
   pi-subagents `status` RPC and feeds the returned `text` to
   `applyWorkflowStatus` (`index.ts:248-260`).
3. `parseWorkflowChildStatuses` (`waterfall.ts:186-199`) extracts the last word
   before the first `, ` on each `Workflow child <key>:` line → e.g.
   `"running"`, `"completed"`, `"failed"`.
4. `laneStateFromStatuses` maps that to a lane state. Terminal → `closeSpan`
   (records `endMs = relNow()`); non-terminal → `setSpanState` (no close).
5. On workflow completion, `handleBuildCompletion`/`handleReviewCompletion`
   call `closeAllOpenSpans(...)`, force-closing any lane still open.
6. Renderer draws `startMs → endMs` and labels `endMs - startMs`.

## Root cause (high confidence)

**Status-token mismatch: pi-subagents reports `"completed"`, the factory only
recognizes `"complete"`.**

- A successfully finished child (`scout`, `plan`) yields `["completed"]` →
  `laneStateFromStatuses` returns `"queued"` (`waterfall.ts:204-209`) →
  `applyWorkflowStatus` takes the `setSpanState` branch (`index.ts:241`), which
  only mutates `state` and leaves `endMs === null`.
- Those lanes therefore never close at their real completion time. When the
  build workflow fails at `implement`, `handleBuildCompletion` runs
  `closeAllOpenSpans("failed")` (`index.ts:507`), stamping **every** open lane
  with the same `relNow()` — the failure instant. That is the shared right edge
  (~20m) and the reason `scout` shows `20m08s` and `plan` `19m29s` rather than
  their true durations.
- `implement` was the lane that actually failed acceptance; its lane is closed
  at the same failure instant (either by a poll seeing `"failed"` → `closeSpan`,
  or by the `closeAllOpenSpans` fallback). Its displayed duration reflects
  "start-of-first-observation → failure moment", not the true work window.

This also directly answers the user's report (a): implement's end time is never
written at its own completion; it is force-written later at the failure moment.
There is no path that records a per-child true end timestamp — ends are always
"now when we noticed".

Corroborating internal inconsistency: the same repo already treats the finished
status as `"completed"` in `state.ts`/`state.test.ts`, but the live-status
parser and its tests use `"complete"` (`waterfall.test.ts:155,161,170-173`), so
the bug is untested.

Secondary issues found:
- `openSpan` is called unconditionally *before* the state check
  (`index.ts:240`), so a child first observed as already finished would be
  opened at `relNow()` and (if the token were recognized) immediately closed at
  `relNow()` → near-zero span. Start times are "first poll that mentions the
  child", not the child's real start.
- `openSpan` never refines `startMs` on later observations (`index.ts:176`).
- Axis scaling uses `model.nowMs = relNow()` at each refresh (`index.ts:206`,
  `:804`); after a failed run is viewed later via `/factory-status`, `nowMs`
  grows past `maxEnd`, shrinking all bars toward the left. Not the primary bug
  but amplifies the "spans look wrong" impression.
- `laneStateFromStatuses` also ignores `"detached"`, `"rejected"`, `"partial"`
  (in `WorkflowNodeStatus`), which would likewise fall through to `"queued"`.

## Exact banner path (question 4)
- Event: `pi.events.on(ASYNC_COMPLETE_EVENT, ...)` — `index.ts:659`, event name
  `"subagent:async-complete"` (`index.ts:63`).
- Dispatches to `handleBuildCompletion` when `isBuild` (`index.ts:677`).
- Failure branch: `index.ts:503-510`:
  ```ts
  503  if (payload.success === false || payload.stopped === true ||
           payload.timedOut === true || payload.interrupted === true) {
  504      state.phase = "failed";
  505      state.error = `build workflow did not complete (state: ${...}, summary: ${boundedSummary(payload.summary)}).`;
  507      closeAllOpenSpans("failed");   // <-- all open lanes snapshot endMs = relNow()
  ```
  So lane end times are snapshotted **only at this moment**, for every lane that
  was never correctly closed — which (per the mismatch above) is all of them.

## Gaps / uncertainty
- I did not capture a live `status` RPC text; the `"completed"` token is
